text:
elaine: FYI, CI gate just flagged a big mem/perf regression after the slab-coalescer merge (commit d4f2a9c). Longctx tests are OOMing in 80% of workers at seqlen 2048 :grimacing:
ci-bot: [build 2197] https://ci/internal/builds/2197 - failed tests: perf/longctx-2048 (OOM). Logs attached.
elaine: quick paste from pprof (staging replica) - top of heap:
```
(pprof) top10
  32.2MB  62.3% 62.3%  runtime.mallocgc
  10.8MB  20.9% 83.2%  slab_coalescer.merge_blocks
   5.4MB  10.5% 93.7%  kv::cache::insert
```
Looks like the coalescer slow path allocs are up.
michael: can you repro locally on a dev box? bisect candidate range? :eyes:
elaine: repros in docker with the same workload. bisect plan: test revert range between merge PR #4521 and the batching tweak PR #4510. starting binary search now.
raj: ran microbench on my workstation, results: median latency @ seqlen 512 unchanged, @ 1024 +12% p95, @2048 +28% p95. flamegraph points at `slab_coalescer::try_merge` hotpath.
sophie: hunch: merge increases slab coalescing attempts which interacts poorly with the eviction fastpath at high seqlen -> fragmentation + extra allocs. Could be that our kernel selection is picking "slowpath" kernels for merged slabs.
elaine: also noticing increased continuous-batch sizes in the logs when coalescer is enabled, maybe batching heuristic mis-estimates batchable token boundaries.
michael: if it's blocking canary rollout we should hold release. ops-bot, can you gate the rollout?
ops-bot: Rollout hold applied to release/2024.03.14 on canaries. :no_entry_sign: All canary rollouts paused.
elaine: running targeted perf profile w/ `--perf-flame -s 2048` and preparing minimal reproducer.
raj: tried a local build with the coalescer toggled off, memory stable, no OOM, p95 back to baseline. This narrows to coalescer changes + interaction with eviction.
sophie: suggestion: as a mitigation, disable slab coalescer on seqlen >= 1024 or force kernel fallback to legacy allocator while we investigate. That should be cheap to flip.
michael: agree. If we can't hotfix quickly, revert PR #4521. Which is lower blast radius?
elaine: attempting quick config flag: `coalescer.enabled=true` -> flip to false for longctx. Pushing patch to staging config now.
ci-bot: config update rolled to staging: https://config/internal/changes/789 :white_check_mark:
elaine: staging run after config flip: no OOMs, mem profile looks like:
```
(pprof) top10
  12.1MB  24.4% 24.4%  runtime.mallocgc
   4.3MB   8.7% 33.1%  kv::cache::insert
```
good signal.
michael: still want a revert PR to be safe for prod. raj can you open revert?
raj: opened revert PR #4567 (revert: slab-coalescer). link: https://git.internal/r/4567. Marking as revert-only, no other changes.
sophie: I'll prepare an alternate patch that gates coalescer by seqlen and forces kernel fallback for merged slabs; maybe lower perf hit but safer.
elaine: running a bisect to pinpoint exact commit in the merge chain, will post results.
raj: post-merge revert smoke on canaries shows memory stable and no perf regression. ops-bot, please allow rollout resume once revert merges.
ops-bot: Canary resume gated on CI green for revert PR. Notifying release leads.
michael: long-term, add a regression test covering slab coalescer + eviction interaction at high seqlen in our perf CI. Add to perf/regression/longctx.
sophie: agreed, also add a flamegraph assertion or leak detector in the test harness.
elaine: bisect result: problematic commit is d4f2a9c (part of PR #4521) where `merge_block_threshold` was lowered and `coalesce_attempts` loop was changed. Will include repro steps in PR comment.
elaine: merging revert now, will monitor prod canaries closely. Thanks everyone. :heart:
